title: KernelEvolve: Scaling Agentic Kernel Coding for Heterogeneous AI Accelerators at Meta

mechanism.domainTask: Production-scale Triton kernel generation and optimization across NVIDIA, AMD, and Meta MTIA accelerators
mechanism.populationDetail: Kernel artifacts are stored in an explicit parent-child search graph/tree; evolutionary search configurations also maintain diverse flat candidate populations, while greedy/MCTS modes operate over tree nodes.
mechanism.archiveDetail: The paper persists candidates and retrieves high-performing ancestors but does not specify a separate elite archive or archive admission rule common across search modes.
mechanism.replacementDetail: Candidate artifacts are persisted as graph nodes; search state may prune nodes in context-dependent ways, but there is no universal bounded survivor policy.
mechanism.generationDetail: A universal operator transforms a selected existing kernel using a current optimization context; transformations may be broad or targeted and are not limited to localized patches.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: Evaluator returns correctness, speedup, compiler/runtime diagnostics, and multi-level profiling; artifacts and analysis reports are persisted and reused for subsequent tree expansion.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: Search policies choose nodes/subsets for expansion; persistent context memory can retrieve high-performing related kernels across prior searches. Exact parent count and default selection rule are unspecified.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: A production workflow combines heterogeneous model backends, persistent cross-run hardware knowledge, dynamic retrieval agents, and remote accelerator evaluation as one kernel-generation service.

provenance.sourcePdf: papers/KernelEvolve Scaling Agentic Kernel Coding for Heterogeneous AI Accelerators at Meta.pdf
provenance.citationWarning: Survey already covers tree structure, prompt context, metadata, async evaluation, scalar objective, and deployment. Clarify that greedy/MCTS/evolutionary search are supported alternatives; do not imply a single simultaneous hybrid unless a deployment configuration confirms it. Backend list does not establish dynamic model routing or collaboration. No universal elite archive policy is described.
